t: Enthroned at seven and ruling through regents until 1669, the Kangxi Emperor reigned for 61 years, the longest reign of any Chinese emperor.

He put down the Revolt of the Three Feudatories in 1681, took Taiwan in 1683, agreed a border with Russia at Nerchinsk in 1689 and fought the Dzungars in Mongolia and Tibet, with severe measures against some of those who resisted.
His later years were marked by a succession dispute among his sons, and historians still debate whether the Yongzheng Emperor took the throne legitimately.
dyk: Thomas Pereira taught the Kangxi Emperor to play the harpsichord, and he was the first Chinese emperor to play a western musical instrument.
ev: Xuanye, the future Kangxi Emperor, is born in the Forbidden City in Beijing
He is enthroned at the age of seven, with four regents holding actual power
He has the regent Oboi arrested and begins to take personal control of the empire
Qing forces end the Revolt of the Three Feudatories, which had lasted eight years
The Qing admiral Shi Lang defeats the Kingdom of Tungning off Penghu, and Taiwan becomes part of the Qing Empire
The Treaty of Nerchinsk fixes a border between Russia and China
Pope Clement XI condemns the Chinese rites, and Kangxi forbids Christian missions in China
The Kangxi Emperor dies, and his fourth son Yinzhen succeeds as the Yongzheng Emperor

f.born: 4 May 1654 in Jingren Palace, the Forbidden City, Beijing, as Xuanye; third son of the Shunzhi Emperor and Empress Xiaokangzhang
f.died: 20 December 1722; buried at the Eastern Tombs in Zunhua, Hebei
f.role: Third emperor of the Qing dynasty, enthroned 7 February 1661 at the age of seven; under regents until he took personal control in 1669; reigned 61 years, until 1722
f.known: the longest reign of any Chinese emperor; the suppression of the Revolt of the Three Feudatories; the annexation of Taiwan in 1683; the Treaty of Nerchinsk with Russia; campaigns against the Dzungars; the Kangxi Dictionary and other great compilations; the Chinese Rites controversy; the succession dispute among his sons
